title: Rabbi Elazar ben Dalgai
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Mishnah Tamid, chapter 3, mishnah 8, where he said: "My father's household had goats on Mount Mikhvar, and they would sneeze from the smell of the incense compound." There, in the Mishnah, the reading is 'ben Dagla'i'; but in the Western (Palestinian) text the reading is 'ben Dalga'i', and so it appears in the Jerusalem Talmud, Sukkah chapter 5, halakhah 3; and in Yoma 39b the reading is 'ben Dolga'i', and some read there 'Rabbi Yose ben Dolga'i'.

In the newspaper "Hashkafah," year 7, issue 32, Rabbi Baruch Chuma of Jerusalem writes that he found in a Bomberg edition of the Mishnah, printed in Venice in the year 5288 [1527–1528], the text: "Rabbi Elazar said: two dalgei of goats..." etc. He conjectures that the first copyist wrote 'two dalgei izim' (taking dalgei to mean flocks), and the second copyist came and wrote 'ben Dalgei.' Hyman acknowledges it as a clever suggestion, but finds it very difficult to emend in four places. Likewise, we would also have to emend and say 'Rabbi Eliezer', since Rabbi Elazar (ben Shamua) was not in the time of the Temple; furthermore, Hyman does not find anywhere in the Talmud the word 'dalgei' used for flocks of sheep.

notes.text: The proposed reading “two dalgei of goats” takes dalgei as flocks; Hyman rejects the conjecture and says that meaning is otherwise unattested in the Talmud. His four-location objection and Elazar/Eliezer chronology argument remain his own. The year5288 spans1527–1528.

The inspected Mishnah Tamid 3:8 reads Rabbi Eliezer ben Diglai; the inspected Yoma 39b reads Rabbi (Yose ben) Dulgai. These differ from Hyman’s Elazar and Daglai/Dalgai forms. The precise Bomberg printing and Hashkafah article were not inspected; Hyman’s four-location objection, Elazar/Eliezer chronology and rejection of the two-dalgei conjecture remain his own.
